clue.text: Poor relationship that could be almost cowardly

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters may be rearranged into something else
almost means the word falls one letter short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone describes a feeble, faint-hearted partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of cowardly, leaving COWARDL; 'could be' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cold War was the long hostile standoff between the USA and USSR, a notably bad relationship between states.

clue.text: Base with firm bottom

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
arse is British slang for the backside

explanation.surface: A foundation built on solid ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like a foundation but means vulgar; 'bottom' is the rude British word for the buttocks, not a foundation's underside.
explanation.definitionFit: Base in the sense of low and vulgar is a synonym of crude or unrefined.

clue.text: Dislike of bad language in the French

indicators.note: in places the swear word inside the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
an oath is a swear word, a piece of bad language

explanation.surface: Someone objects to swearing in French.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislike strongly is to detest or abhor something.

clue.text: Conveyance preparatory to interment

parts.note: sounds like a hearse carrying a body to a funeral, but it is the wheeled container that takes rubbish off to be buried in landfill

explanation.walkthrough: The funereal language suggests a hearse; the interment is of household rubbish in a landfill site.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeled rubbish bin carries household waste to the kerb before it is taken away and buried at a tip.

clue.text: Wars of heaving sores

indicators.note: heaving suggests the letters are tossed and churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Battles fought by people with throbbing sores.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wars of the Roses were the fifteenth-century English civil wars between York and Lancaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The English civil wars of York and Lancaster are known by this flower name, completing the phrase.

clue.text: Help paper to bed in formal cover

indicators.note: in places the bed inside the formal outfit

parts.note: a suit is formal clothing that covers the body
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone puts a newspaper to bed while dressed up formally.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit copy for a newspaper is to assist in preparing the paper for print.

clue.text: Shopkeeper burst into tears

indicators.note: burst suggests the letters are blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper suddenly starts crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst' looks like part of 'burst into tears', but it is the anagram signal on the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer is a retailer who sells paper, pens and office supplies.

clue.text: Rise makes young man about turn

indicators.note: about means the boy goes around the turn

parts.note: a boy is a young male
a U-turn, so U stands for turn

explanation.surface: Something prompts a youth to rise and turn around.
explanation.definitionFit: To buoy, or buoy up, is to keep afloat or lift, so it means rise.

clue.text: Preparation of horse for time under cover

indicators.note: under, in a down clue, puts the time below the cover

parts.note: to dress is to clothe or cover
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Getting a horse ready while it waits under a rug.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the training of a horse to perform precise movements, its schooling for competition.

clue.text: Go without a garment in parody

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the attempt surrounds the clothing

parts.note: a go is an attempt, a try
a vest is an undergarment

explanation.surface: Someone goes undressed in a comic send-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' a garment, but here it carries its old sense of outside, so it signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque imitation or mockery, much like a burlesque.

clue.text: Shell has vehicle going swiftly

indicators.note: has means the shell word contains the vehicle followed by the rest, so removing the vehicle leaves the remainder

parts.note: a carapace is the hard upper shell of a crab or tortoise
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A shell-branded vehicle speeding along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell' tempts as the oil company; it is CARAPACE, which is CAR plus the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace is an adverb meaning quickly or at speed.

clue.text: Note a father with time for what's on TV

parts.note: so (soh) is a note of the sol-fa scale
pop is an informal word for father
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A note from a father about time spent watching television.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running serial drama is a staple of television schedules.

clue.text: Chic lost as turning to bluestocking?

definitions.note: a learned woman, so the adjective describing her is studious and academic

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters revolve into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A fashionable person abandons style to become a learned woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluestocking is an intellectual woman, and scholastic describes academic, learned pursuits.

clue.text: Area of land would have added value in West London

indicators.note: would have added means the answer plus the value word gives the place, so take that word away

parts.note: Isleworth is a district of West London, in the borough of Hounslow
worth means value

explanation.surface: A plot of land would be worth more in West London.
explanation.walkthrough: ISLEWORTH is a district of West London; add WORTH (value) to the answer and you get it.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, a piece of land surrounded by water.

clue.text: Mrs Mop works after hours without conviction

parts.note: Mrs Mop is a British nickname for a cleaning lady, so her work is she cleans
late means after the usual hours

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady works overtime, half-heartedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without conviction' reads as half-hearted, but means having no criminal record.
explanation.definitionFit: A record free of criminal convictions is spotless, a fresh start with nothing against one's name.

clue.text: Important character — it's heavy (in gravity, not so)

parts.note: leading as in made of lead, the proverbially heavy metal
light means not heavy in weight

explanation.surface: A grave and weighty figure who is somehow also not weighty.
explanation.walkthrough: LEADING here means made of lead, hence heavy; LIGHT is its opposite, 'not so' heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading light is a prominent, influential person in a field.

clue.text: It's easy to call in doctor with a stroke

indicators.note: in places the doctor and a within the easy task

parts.note: a doddle is British slang for an easy task
GP is a general practitioner, a doctor

explanation.surface: Calling the doctor about a stroke is simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stroke' suggests a medical emergency, but it is a swimming stroke; a doddle is British slang for something easy.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog paddle is a simple swimming stroke, paddling with the hands like a dog.

clue.text: Devotion with no right to be allied to autism

indicators.note: with no means the right is taken away from the condition's name

parts.note: Asperger's is a form of autism

explanation.surface: Devotion without rightness is linked to autism.
explanation.definitionFit: The Asperges is a Roman Catholic rite of sprinkling holy water before Mass, a devotional ceremony.

clue.text: Composer takes part backing single

parts.note: J. S. Bach the composer

indicators.note: backing means the word for part runs backwards

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: A composer plays a supporting role on a single release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single' looks like a record release but means an unmarried man.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried man is single.

clue.text: Shriek about owning toiletry

indicators.note: about means the shriek goes around the possession word

parts.note: a scream is a shriek
having means owning

explanation.surface: Someone screams over possessing a bathroom product.
explanation.definitionFit: Lather applied to the face before using a razor is a bathroom product.

clue.text: Like a time bomb, something given without prior notice

indicators.note: without means the gift loses a letter

parts.note: a present is a gift

indicators.note: prior picks the first letter of notice

explanation.surface: A gift is handed over without warning.
explanation.definitionFit: A time bomb is set in advance to go off at a fixed moment.

clue.text: One begins a test with need for bottle

definitions.meaning: in cricket, an opening batsman starts a Test match innings
a bottle needs a tool to remove its cap

explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match; the opening batsman begins it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an opening batsman and a bottle-top remover take this name, from starting or unsealing.

clue.text: How Israelis used to measure a messy heap?

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a noun, the ancient unit they used

indicators.note: messy suggests the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Ancient Israelites measuring a disorderly pile.
explanation.definitionFit: The epha was an ancient Hebrew dry measure, about a bushel.

clue.text: Observe band keeping time?

parts.note: to watch is to observe
a strap is a band

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on the band that keeps time.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is wordplay and, with 'keeping time?', a description of the band on a wristwatch.
explanation.definitionFit: The band holding a timepiece to the wrist is this strap.

clue.text: Deliver state victory

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state
VE is Victory in Europe

explanation.surface: A state delivers victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows calve, delivering their young.

clue.text: Vocative fellows get a warning

parts.note: O is the vocative exclamation, as in O God
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Men addressed directly receive a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent or sign of what is to come is a warning.

clue.text: Model glad to work for a symbol of achievement

indicators.note: to work means the letters are put to work and reshaped

explanation.surface: A model happy to work for an award.
explanation.definitionFit: First prize in Olympic competition is the top award, emblem of success.

clue.text: Priest not soft on crime

indicators.note: not means the soft letter is dropped

parts.note: a parson is a priest
p (piano) means soft in music

explanation.surface: A priest who is not soft on crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Gin's in season at early evening

parts.note: spring is a season

indicators.note: early picks the first letter of evening

explanation.surface: Gin is in season early in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' looks like the drink; it is a snare, as is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a trap, and a springe is a noose snare for catching small game.

clue.text: English reader, occasionally getting a choice

parts.note: a lector is a reader, especially in church

explanation.surface: An English reader sometimes gets to choose.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter gets a choice at the occasional election.
